source.title: Open Source Automated Interpretability for Sparse Autoencoder Features

page_placements.theme: Explanations fitted to top-activating examples (of SAE features, vision units and some neurons) predict activation over the rest of the range only partly

record.tranche_reason: The post evaluates whether explanations of SAE features predict activation on other examples, and reports cases where explanations based on top activations generalize poorly. This is a refinement of claims about how much feature explanations establish.
record.gate_note: The experiments concern sparse-autoencoder features, not the model's own neurons or neuron poles. Results are relevant to explanation fidelity and generalization, but do not directly establish how many neurons have one or two jobs.
record.test_reason: All results concern sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features of GPT-2, Llama-3 8b and Pythia, not the model's own neurons. Every version names neurons or neuron poles, so no version is tested. The post cites Bills et al. (an original source) and correlates its scores with simulation scoring (r=0.61), but reports no neuron-level shares or simulation-score distribution. Its findings on explanation generalization are an SAE-feature analogue of V6 and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add: explanations fail to distinguish neighbouring features (detection falls to near random), and output-type features are uninterpretable from activations and need causal scoring. All conclusions are about SAE features, not neurons.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses language models to generate and score natural-language explanations of SAE features, with detection and fuzzing evaluations; it does not audit neuron poles.
record.method_sensitivity: Explanation quality varies with activation strength and with how activating examples are sampled; scoring also varies with evaluator model size.

fits_no_version.finding: For GPT-2 SAE features, explanations built from only the top activating examples are narrower and score worse on detection and fuzzing across the activation distribution than explanations built from examples sampled across it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature explanations formed from top activations fail to predict weaker activations (an SAE analogue of V6).

fits_no_version.finding: Weak activations (low deciles) are harder to score and less related to the feature's apparent concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature explanation accuracy declines toward low activation deciles.

fits_no_version.finding: Detection balanced accuracy falls from >80% to about random when the non-activating examples come from neighbouring features (Appendix, Figure S1). Explanations are not specific enough to separate similar contexts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature explanations lack precision against near-neighbour counterexamples.

fits_no_version.finding: Some late-circuit Pythia SAE features fire on dense, unrelated tokens and are explainable only through their output logits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some features are not explainable from activating examples and need causal scoring.

record.problems: The results concern SAE features rather than individual neurons. Several relevant comparisons are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. The authors note that weak activations are harder to score and that fuzzing fails to classify incorrectly marked examples.
record.rows_left_out: Other SAE-pipeline results, including feature filtering, generation scoring, and scorer comparisons, were not included because they do not directly test whether explanations formed from activating examples predict where individual neurons fire. Figure 4 rows are retained as a separate generalization result.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed because V6 concerns neuron explanations and the study measures SAE features only. There are no instructions in the text.

relation.reason: The post cites Bills et al. and discusses simulation scoring's bias toward recall. It also correlates its scores with simulation scoring (r=0.61). It reports no neuron results. The reader's 'tests' call is wrong.

tranche.reason: All results are on SAE features (GPT-2, Llama-3 8b, Pythia), not neurons or neuron poles. No version is tested. The reader's T5 call is wrong.

source_check.notes: All five rows are figure-only values on SAE features. The decile, top-versus-whole-distribution and neighbour results are analogues of V6, not tests of it. The r4/r5 verdict fix calls the Figure 4 features 'hand-picked', but the text says they were randomly selected from layers 0-2.

statements.problem: No error. Minor: the text names no model for appendix Figure S1, so the 'GPT-2' heading is likely but not confirmed for f2.
